subject: literature
passage: In the twelve years Amos Pruitt had kept the telegraph office at Linden Falls, he had learned to read the town's fortunes in the clatter of the sounder before he had written out a single word. Grain prices came in brisk and businesslike; weddings arrived in a cheerful, careless rhythm. The message that began coming through that October afternoon came slowly, as if the operator at the other end were reluctant to send it. <u>Amos laid down his pencil before the last word was finished, for he knew already whose name it would carry.</u> He sat a long while in the yellow light of the window, and when at last he rose to put on his coat, he walked to the Lindqvists' house by the longest road in town.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It introduces a long-standing conflict between Amos and the family he must visit.
choices.B: It marks the moment when Amos first discovers that he can interpret a message's rhythm.
choices.C: It shows Amos's long-practiced skill applied to a message whose meaning he dreads.
choices.D: It reveals that Amos misreads the message because the operator sends it too slowly.

explanation.why: The first sentence establishes that over "twelve years" Amos has learned to read news from the rhythm of the sounder. In the underlined sentence he stops writing because "he knew already" what the slow message means. What follows (sitting "a long while," taking "the longest road") shows his reluctance, so the sentence applies his skill to news he does not want to deliver.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests any conflict between Amos and the Lindqvists; his slow walk reflects reluctance to bring bad news.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The first sentence says Amos has had this skill for years, so the underlined sentence is not his first discovery of it.
explanation.C: Correct. The sentence draws on the ability described at the start, and the slow walk that follows shows that he dreads the message.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Amos does not misread anything; the slow rhythm is exactly what tells him what the message is about.
